title: Componentwise linear restriction-stalk maps
statement: For every ringed space X, open W and x∈W, there are component linear maps from the restricted module stalk (with transported scalars) to the original stalk, sending every restricted germ to the ambient germ on the image open.

proof.text: Construct an additive cocone from the ambient germs of sections on image opens, verify naturality using germ_res_apply, and descend it by the stalk colimit universal property. The colimit descent formula gives the germ identity. Represent a scalar and a vector on a common intersection and use germ_smul and restrictStalkIso_hom_eq_germ to prove semilinearity; restriction of scalars along the inverse stalk-ring isomorphism then makes the comparison linear.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_moduleRestrictionStalk_components (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (W : Opens X)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ W) :
    ∃ c : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X),
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          (X.toPresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso W.isOpenEmbedding ⟨x, hx⟩).inv.hom).obj
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (X.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding) ⟨x, hx⟩).obj
          ((W.sheafOfModulesEquivOver (moduleRings X)).functor.obj
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X) W).obj F))) ⟶
        (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj F,
      ∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (V : Opens W)
        (hV : (⟨x, hx⟩ : W) ∈ V)
        (s : F.val.obj (op (W.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap.functor.obj V))),
        (c F) (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u})
          (X := (X.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding).carrier)
          ((W.sheafOfModulesEquivOver (moduleRings X)).functor.obj
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X) W).obj F)).val.presheaf
          V ⟨x, hx⟩ hV s) =
        TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X.carrier) F.val.presheaf
          (W.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap.functor.obj V) x ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hV, rfl⟩ s

mathlib_searches.query: A family of module stalk maps specified on germs commutes with the maps induced by morphisms of sheaves
The stalk of a module sheaf restricted to an open subspace agrees with its original stalk, compatibly with the stalk ring action
